behentrimonium-chloride.text: Behentrimonium chloride is the waxy conditioning agent in many hair conditioners, used to make hair slippery, easier to detangle and less static so it looks smoother and sleeker. It is a background formulation ingredient rather than a standalone treatment, and it has not been tested on its own for appearance outcomes.

polyquaternium-10.text: Polyquaternium-10 is a cationic polymer in shampoos and conditioners that coats the hair, helping with combing, softness and manageability so hair looks smoother after washing. It appears as a background ingredient in hair-care products; there are no dedicated trials of it for appearance.

cetrimonium-chloride.text: Cetrimonium chloride is a common conditioner ingredient used to detangle and soften hair, giving a smoother, more manageable look after washing. Users of conditioners get this effect as part of the whole formula; the ingredient itself has not been studied for appearance outcomes, and contact-allergy reports are documented.

keratin-straightening.text: Keratin straightening, or a Brazilian treatment, is a salon service used to reduce frizz and add shine, with results lasting roughly two to six months. The smoother look is visible right after the session; controlled trial data on the treatment are limited.

japanese-thermal-reconditioning.text: Japanese thermal reconditioning (yuko or rebonding) is a salon process used to permanently straighten curly or wavy hair, giving a sleek, straight look that is visible immediately and stays in treated hair. No clinical trials were found; its use rests on salon practice and client experience.

sodium-hydroxide-relaxer.text: A sodium hydroxide (lye) relaxer is the classic cream used to permanently straighten tight curls, giving a straight, smooth look in treated hair that is visible straight away; new growth comes in with its natural texture. Its straightening effect is well established in practice, while broader health associations are still under study.

calcium-hydroxide-relaxer.text: Calcium hydroxide 'no-lye' relaxers are used to permanently straighten tight curls and are marketed as an option for sensitive scalps. The straightening is visible right after treatment; the claim of a gentler profile than lye relaxers has not been shown in studies.

chain: Hair conditioned and held in place
macassar-oil.text: Macassar oil was a Victorian-era hair oil used by men to condition and style hair, giving a glossy, neat finish that is visible when applied. It was also advertised as promoting regrowth, a claim that rests on historical marketing rather than clinical trials.

jaw-surgery-orthognathic.text: Orthognathic surgery repositions the upper jaw, lower jaw and chin, and forum users treat it as the major structural option for a recessed jaw, facial balance and a straighter bite and smile. The change in jaw position is itself the visible result; reports note that functional gains and cosmetic outcomes do not always match.

low-glycemic-diet-for-acne.text: People with acne adopt a low-glycemic diet hoping that steadier blood sugar will reduce breakouts and give clearer skin. It is among the few diet changes with some trial support for acne, though the evidence is modest.
